<!-- head-1: body_md -->
Since \eqref{eq:warp} preserves the zero-crossing event, warped-GP quantiles \cite{snelson2003} and the Gaussian deterministic equivalent \cite{nemirovski2006}, also used for an unwarped GP in \cite{divito2026}, give the exact equivalence under the fitted posterior
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P_{\mathcal D}\{y(\bm x)\ge0\}&\ge1-\varepsilon\\
\Longleftrightarrow\quad\mu_g(\bm x)-z_{1-\varepsilon}\sigma_g(\bm x)&\ge0,
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:chance_equivalent}
\end{equation}
where $z_{1-\varepsilon}=\Phi^{-1}(1-\varepsilon)$ and $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function.
<!-- end head-1 -->
